title: 马来西亚大学生宽带推荐：合租房便宜 Fibre 配套怎么选
content:
如果你是在马来西亚大学附近租房，和 4–8 名学生一起合租，选 Broadband 不应该只看 Mbps；合约多久、Fibre 覆盖、Upload Speed、Wi-Fi 和每个人实际分摊多少钱，同样重要。

学生合租房需要多少 Mbps？

可以先按照人数这样估算：

  1. 1–2人： 100–200Mbps
  2. 3–4人： 200–300Mbps
  3. 5–8人： 300–500Mbps

这只是实际使用上的参考，并不是硬性标准。

例如，4个人如果只是上课、刷网页和看 YouTube，300Mbps 已经相当充裕；但如果同时有人打游戏、Netflix 4K、Steam 下载大型游戏，甚至多人进行 Video Call，网络压力就会明显增加。

所以合租 Broadband 真正需要考虑的是同时使用人数和使用方式。

学生合租 Broadband 怎么选？TIME、Unifi、Maxis 比较

学生选 Broadband，不能只比较月费。最好一起看 Download / Upload Speed、合约期限、地址覆盖和人均成本。

Provider推荐配套月费Download / Upload合约适合谁
TIME Fibre200Mbps / 600MbpsRM119 / RM159200/200Mbps、600/500MbpsStudent Plan 12个月想要短合约和高 Upload Speed 的学生
Unifi300Mbps / 500MbpsRM129 / RM149300/50Mbps、500/100Mbps长期合约，具体以当前优惠为准地址有覆盖、多人合租
Maxis Fibre300Mbps / 500MbpsRM139 / RM159以申请时最新配套为准24个月或更长，视配套而定已经使用 Maxis Postpaid 或符合 Bundle 条件的学生

TIME 目前提供专门的 Student Plans，200Mbps 为 RM119/月、600Mbps 为 RM159/月，并提供 12个月合约；学生申请需要 Student ID。（Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students）

Unifi 目前的 300Mbps 配套为 RM129/月，500Mbps 为 RM149/月，对应 Upload Speed 分别为 50Mbps 和 100Mbps。目前官网相关配套页面显示 27个月合约，但优惠活动可能调整合约条件。（Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Shield / Unifi Home Fibre Plans）

Maxis 目前标准 Home Fibre 价格中，300Mbps 为 RM139/月，500Mbps 为 RM159/月。合约期限会根据具体配套和促销而不同，申请前应该确认当时的 T&C。（Source: Maxis — Maxis Home Fibre Plans）

最重要的一点： Broadband Coverage 是看具体地址，不是看“这所大学附近有没有 Fibre”。

TIME Fibre：如果你家有覆盖，学生很值得考虑

TIME 对学生最大的吸引力之一，是目前提供 12个月 Student Plan。

200Mbps 是 RM119/月，提供 200Mbps Download 和 200Mbps Upload；600Mbps 是 RM159/月，提供 600Mbps Download 和 500Mbps Upload。（Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students）

对于合租房来说，高 Upload Speed 对以下使用场景比较有帮助：

  1. 上传 Assignment
  2. Google Drive / OneDrive 同步
  3. Video Call
  4. 上传大型文件
  5. Cloud Backup
  6. 一边 Gaming、一边进行其他网络活动

如果你的租约也是一年左右，12个月 Broadband Contract 会比 24个月甚至更长的合约容易规划。

但 TIME 最大的问题也很直接：不是每个学生公寓或租屋地址都有覆盖。

Unifi：多人合租的实际选择

Unifi 300Mbps 和 500Mbps 对多人合租来说都是比较常见的选择。

目前 300Mbps 为 RM129/月，Upload 50Mbps；500Mbps 为 RM149/月，Upload 100Mbps。（Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Shield）

问题主要在于合约期限。

目前 Unifi 相关配套页面显示 27个月合约，因此如果你只租一年，这一点必须认真考虑。（Source: Unifi — 300Mbps / 500Mbps Home Fibre Plans）

搬家时可能面对：

  1. 转移 Broadband
  2. 提前终止合约
  3. 继续支付剩余合约费用
  4. 寻找新的租户接手（如果条款允许）

所以不要只看 RM129 或 RM149 的月费。

Maxis Fibre：如果你本身用 Maxis，可以一起算

Maxis 目前标准 Home Fibre 价格为：

  1. 300Mbps：RM139/月
  2. 500Mbps：RM159/月
  3. 1Gbps：RM249/月

新安装配套目前也包括 WiFi 6 Router。（Source: Maxis — Maxis Home Fibre FAQ）

如果你已经是 Maxis Postpaid 用户，还可以看看 Fibre Bundle。

符合条件的 Maxis Postpaid 用户目前有机会获得 Bundle 优惠，例如 500Mbps 和 1Gbps 的组合价格会比标准 Fibre 月费更低。（Source: Maxis — Maxis Postpaid + Fibre Bundle）

但不要只看 Fibre 的价格。

应该计算：

Mobile Plan + Fibre = 每个月实际需要支付多少钱

如果你本来就需要 Maxis 手机配套，Bundle 可能有意义；如果只是为了 Fibre 特意加入 Postpaid，则需要重新计算。

8人合租真正容易出问题的地方

假设你们8个人共用一条 500Mbps Fibre。

晚上8点：

  1. A 在打 Online Game
  2. B 在 Google Meet 上课
  3. C 在看 Netflix
  4. D 在看 YouTube
  5. E 正在 Steam 下载游戏
  6. F 正在上传 Assignment
  7. G、H 在刷网页和社交媒体

这时候问题未必是“500Mbps 不够”。

真正的问题可能是 Router Queue 被大量下载或上传流量塞满。

结果就是：

Steam 下载很快，但游戏 Ping 突然飙高。

这时候升级到更高 Mbps 未必是最有效的解决方案，先处理 Router Traffic Management 反而可能更实际。

什么是 QoS？

QoS（Quality of Service） 是 Router 用来管理网络流量的功能。

它不会把 300Mbps 变成 500Mbps。

它的作用是：当网络发生拥塞时，让重要流量先得到处理。

对于 Gaming 来说，这一点尤其重要，因为游戏通常更在意：

稳定的 Latency > 超高 Download Speed

例如一条 300Mbps Fibre，只要 QoS 和 Router 配置合理，在多人同时使用时，也可能比一条速度更高但经常被大型下载占满的网络体验更好。

💡 NetBijak 推荐的 Router QoS 规则

🎮 NetBijak Recommended Router QoS Rules
🔴 HIGH PRIORITY
  1. Gaming PC / Console
  2. Zoom / Google Meet
  3. Microsoft Teams
🟡 NORMAL PRIORITY
  1. Web Browsing
  2. University Canvas / Moodle
  3. Email
  4. YouTube / Netflix
🟢 LOW PRIORITY
  1. Steam / Epic Game Downloads
  2. BT / P2P Downloads
  3. Large Cloud Backups
  4. OS Updates

不要把所有设备都设置成 HIGH PRIORITY。

如果所有东西都是 High Priority，就等于没有真正进行优先级管理。

如果你使用的是 300/50Mbps，可以把 QoS 的带宽上限先设置在实际最高速度以下，例如：

  1. Download：约 270–285Mbps
  2. Upload：约 45–47Mbps

这只是实际配置时可以尝试的起点，并不是所有 Router 都应该使用完全相同的数值。

Wi-Fi 差，也会让 Fibre 看起来很慢

即使 Fibre 本身速度正常，Wi-Fi 也可能成为瓶颈。

尤其是：

  1. 双层排屋
  2. 大型公寓
  3. 厚水泥墙
  4. Router 放在客厅角落
  5. 8个人同时连接

如果主要是 Gaming，Ethernet Cable 通常比 Wi-Fi 更稳定。

如果无法拉网线，可以考虑：

  1. 把 Router 放在房子的中央
  2. 使用 Mesh Wi-Fi
  3. 避免把 Router 放进柜子或封闭空间

如果问题是 Wi-Fi Coverage，单纯把 300Mbps 升到 500Mbps 不一定能解决问题。

学生应该用 Fibre 还是 5G Home WiFi？

如果只是短租几个月，5G Home WiFi 的确有吸引力。

它比较适合：

  1. 租期很短
  2. 房屋没有 Fibre
  3. 需要快速安装
  4. 经常搬家

但 5G 的表现会受到以下因素影响：

  1. 室内 Signal Strength
  2. 附近 5G Cell Site
  3. 网络拥塞
  4. 建筑物结构
  5. 使用时间

如果你是多人合租，而且有人 Gaming、Video Call、下载大型文件，只要地址有 Fibre，通常还是优先考虑 Fibre。

另外，5G Home Internet 可能涉及 CGNAT / Private IP，部分 Gaming、Remote Access、Hosting 或 Port Forwarding 场景可能会受到影响。

租一年，为什么合约长度这么重要？

假设你的租约只有12个月。

但 Broadband Contract 是：

24个月甚至27个月。

你搬家时就可能面对额外成本。

因此，学生选 Broadband 时，应该把：

租屋期限 ≈ Broadband 合约期限

作为一个重要条件。

这也是为什么 TIME 的 12个月 Student Plan 对大学生特别值得比较。（Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students）

4–8个人合租，平均每人多少钱？

例如：

RM159 / 8人

= RM19.88/人/月

RM129 / 4人

= RM32.25/人/月

RM159 / 6人

= RM26.50/人/月

所以多人合租时，RM20–RM30 左右一个人的 Broadband 费用其实可以换来一条相当不错的 Fibre。

不过，不能只看人均价格。

如果便宜 RM10，但合约长了一倍、Wi-Fi 覆盖又差，最终未必划算。

租房前一定要问房东这几个问题

签租约之前，建议先确认：

  1. 这个具体地址有没有 Fibre Coverage？
  2. 屋内有没有 Fibre Termination Point？
  3. 之前有没有人安装过 Fibre？
  4. Router 可以放在哪里？
  5. 现在有没有人在使用 Broadband？
  6. 屋内有没有 Ethernet Port？
  7. Broadband 合约由谁负责？

特别是公寓。

不要因为“同一栋楼有人用 Fibre”，就直接假设你的单位一定可以安装。

学生 Broadband 选择 Checklist

选配套时，按照这个顺序检查：

① Fibre Coverage

先查具体租屋地址。

② Contract Length

看看是否和你的租期匹配。

③ Upload Speed

多人使用时，不要只看 Download。

④ Cost Per Person

把月费除以实际分摊人数。

⑤ Router / Wi-Fi

确认 Router 放置位置和覆盖范围。

⑥ QoS

多人合租、Gaming 和大量下载同时发生时，QoS 很有价值。


NetBijak's Take

学生合租选 Broadband，不要从“哪个 Mbps 最高”开始比较。

更实际的顺序是：

Check Fibre Coverage → Check Contract Length → Compare Upload Speed → Calculate Cost Per Person → Check Router/Wi-Fi → Configure QoS

如果你只租一年，12个月 Student Plan 值得优先比较。

如果 TIME 有覆盖，目前的 Student Plan 是很值得检查的选择；如果没有覆盖，再根据地址、合约和 Bundle 条件比较 Unifi 与 Maxis。

对于 6–8人的合租房，与其盲目追求最高 Mbps，不如先确保 Fibre + 合适 Router + QoS 配置正确。

title: Student Broadband Guide: Cheap Internet Options Near Malaysian Universities
content:
If you are renting a house or apartment with other students, the cheapest broadband plan is not always the best choice. For a 4–8 person household, monthly cost per person, contract length, Fibre availability, upload speed and router performance can matter more than simply buying the lowest-priced plan.

How Much Internet Speed Does a Student House Need?

A useful starting point is:

  1. 1–2 students: 100–200Mbps
  2. 3–4 students: 200–300Mbps
  3. 5–8 students: 300–500Mbps

These are practical guidelines, not hard limits. A four-person house where everyone streams 4K video and joins video calls at the same time can put more pressure on the connection than six light users.

For shared accommodation, the bigger issue is usually simultaneous usage. One person downloading a 100GB game can affect everyone else if the router does not manage the traffic properly.

Student Broadband Comparison: TIME vs Unifi vs Maxis

For students, the most important comparison is not just the advertised download speed. Look at the monthly bill, upload speed, contract commitment and how much each person actually pays.

ProviderRecommended PlansMonthly PriceDownload / UploadContractBest for
TIME Fibre200Mbps / 600MbpsRM119 / RM159200/200Mbps, 600/500Mbps12 months with Student IDStudents who want a shorter commitment and strong upload speed
Unifi300Mbps / 500MbpsRM129 / RM149300/50Mbps, 500/100MbpsLong-term commitment; current offers may varyShared houses where the plan is available at the address
Maxis Fibre300Mbps / 500MbpsRM139 / RM159Check current plan details24 months or longer depending on planStudents already using Maxis or eligible for bundle offers

TIME currently advertises dedicated Student Plans with a 12-month contract, including 200Mbps at RM119/month and 600Mbps at RM159/month. Both plans have symmetrical or high upload speeds compared with many mainstream alternatives. A Student ID is required. (Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students)

Unifi currently lists 300Mbps at RM129/month and 500Mbps at RM149/month, with upload speeds of 50Mbps and 100Mbps respectively. Current individual plan pages show a 27-month contract, although contract terms can change with campaigns. (Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Shield / Unifi Home Fibre Plans)

Maxis currently lists 300Mbps at RM139/month and 500Mbps at RM159/month under its standard Home Fibre pricing. Contract terms depend on the applicable plan or promotion, so students should check the exact offer before signing up. (Source: Maxis — Maxis Home Fibre Plans)

Important: Fibre availability is address-specific. A plan that looks perfect on paper is useless if the rented apartment cannot support that service.

TIME Fibre: The Most Student-Friendly Option If Available

TIME is particularly interesting for students because its dedicated Student Plans are designed around a 12-month commitment.

The 200Mbps plan costs RM119/month, while the 600Mbps plan costs RM159/month. The latter provides 600Mbps download and 500Mbps upload. (Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students)

For a shared student house, that upload speed can be useful when several people are:

  1. Uploading assignments
  2. Using Google Drive or OneDrive
  3. Attending video meetings
  4. Streaming
  5. Uploading large files
  6. Gaming while other users are active

The 12-month commitment can also make more sense for students renting for one academic year than signing a substantially longer contract.

The catch is simple: TIME coverage is not available at every address.

Unifi: A Practical Option for Shared Student Houses

Unifi's 300Mbps and 500Mbps plans are suitable for many shared households.

The current 300Mbps plan is RM129/month with 300Mbps download and 50Mbps upload, while the 500Mbps plan is RM149/month with 500Mbps download and 100Mbps upload. Unifi itself positions these plans for households with multiple connected devices. (Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Shield)

For students, the main issue is the contract commitment.

Current Unifi plan pages show 27-month contracts for these plans. That is significantly longer than a typical one-year student rental, so you should check the exact contract before applying. (Source: Unifi — 300Mbps / 500Mbps Home Fibre Plans)

If your tenancy is only 12 months, a long contract can become an important cost consideration.

Maxis Fibre: Worth Checking If You Already Use Maxis

Maxis Fibre lists 300Mbps at RM139/month and 500Mbps at RM159/month under its current standard Home Fibre pricing. New installations also include a WiFi 6 router under the current offering. (Source: Maxis — Maxis Home Fibre FAQ)

Maxis can become more attractive when you are already using Maxis Postpaid because eligible customers may receive bundled pricing.

For example, current Maxis bundle offers include discounted Fibre pricing for eligible Maxis Postpaid customers. (Source: Maxis — Maxis Postpaid + Fibre Bundle)

However, do not assume the bundle automatically makes Maxis cheaper. Calculate the total monthly bill, including the mobile plan you need to maintain eligibility.

The Real Problem in an 8-Person Student House

Imagine eight students sharing a 500Mbps Fibre connection.

At 8pm:

  1. Student A is playing an online game.
  2. Student B is on a Google Meet call.
  3. Student C is watching Netflix.
  4. Student D is watching YouTube.
  5. Student E is downloading a Steam game.
  6. Student F is uploading a large assignment folder.
  7. Students G and H are browsing and using social media.

The Fibre connection may have enough total bandwidth.

But the gaming PC can still experience high latency or packet loss because large downloads and uploads are filling the router's queues.

This is where QoS becomes useful.

What Is QoS?

QoS (Quality of Service) is a router feature that manages traffic when the connection becomes congested.

It does not increase your broadband speed.

Instead, it helps decide which traffic should be served first when multiple devices are competing for the same connection.

For gaming, this matters because stable latency is usually more important than having an enormous download speed.

A 300Mbps connection with good traffic management can provide a better gaming experience than a much faster connection that is constantly saturated by downloads.

💡 NetBijak Recommended Router QoS Rules

🎮 NetBijak Recommended Router QoS Rules
🔴 HIGH PRIORITY
  1. Gaming PC / Console
  2. Zoom / Google Meet
  3. Microsoft Teams
🟡 NORMAL PRIORITY
  1. Web browsing
  2. University Canvas / Moodle
  3. Email
  4. YouTube / Netflix
🟢 LOW PRIORITY
  1. Steam / Epic game downloads
  2. BT / P2P downloads
  3. Large cloud backups
  4. OS updates

Do not make every device HIGH PRIORITY. If everything is prioritised, the router has little meaningful priority management left to perform.

For a 300Mbps connection, you can also configure the QoS bandwidth slightly below the real maximum—for example, around 270–285Mbps download and 45–47Mbps upload on a 300/50Mbps connection. This is a practical starting point, not a universal setting; the ideal value depends on the router and actual line performance.

Wi-Fi Can Still Be the Bottleneck

Even with good Fibre, Wi-Fi can become the weak link.

This is especially common in:

  1. Large apartments
  2. Double-storey student houses
  3. Houses with thick concrete walls
  4. Rooms far from the router
  5. Houses with 8 or more active users

For gaming, use Ethernet whenever practical.

If Ethernet is not possible, consider placing the router in a central location or using a properly configured mesh Wi-Fi system.

Do not assume upgrading from 300Mbps to 500Mbps will automatically fix bad Wi-Fi coverage.

Should Students Buy 5G Home WiFi Instead?

5G Home WiFi can make sense for students who:

  1. Rent for only a few months
  2. Cannot get Fibre at the property
  3. Need an Internet connection quickly
  4. Move frequently

The major advantage is flexibility.

The downside is consistency.

5G performance can change depending on:

  1. Indoor signal strength
  2. Distance from the cell site
  3. Network congestion
  4. Building construction
  5. Time of day

For competitive gaming or a house with heavy simultaneous usage, Fibre is generally the safer option when it is available.

Another consideration is CGNAT/private IP addressing, which can affect some gaming, remote-access, hosting and port-forwarding use cases.

Is a 12-Month Broadband Contract Better for Students?

If your tenancy is only one academic year, a 12-month Fibre plan can be much easier to manage.

Consider this before signing:

Rental period: 12 months

Broadband contract: 24–27 months

That creates a problem when you move out.

You may have to:

  1. Transfer the service
  2. Pay early termination charges
  3. Find someone to take over the service, if permitted
  4. Continue paying after leaving the property

This is why TIME's current 12-month Student Plans can be particularly relevant to university students. (Source: TIME — Time Home Internet for Students)

How Much Does Broadband Cost Per Student?

The monthly bill becomes much easier to justify when several people share it.

For example:

RM159 plan shared by 8 students

RM159 ÷ 8 = RM19.88 per person/month

RM129 plan shared by 4 students

RM129 ÷ 4 = RM32.25 per person/month

RM159 plan shared by 6 students

RM159 ÷ 6 = RM26.50 per person/month

But do not choose purely based on the lowest cost per person.

A cheap plan with poor Wi-Fi coverage, insufficient upload capacity or a contract that extends beyond your tenancy can cost more in the long run.

What Should You Check Before Renting?

Before signing the rental agreement, ask the landlord or previous tenant:

  1. Is Fibre available at this exact address?
  2. Is there already a Fibre termination point in the house?
  3. Where is the current router located?
  4. Is there already an active broadband account?
  5. How long is the broadband contract?
  6. Can the router be placed in a central location?
  7. Are Ethernet ports available in the bedrooms?

The exact address matters because Fibre availability is not determined simply by whether the neighbourhood has Fibre coverage.

Student Broadband Checklist

Before choosing a plan, check these six things:

1. Fibre Coverage

Check the exact rental address, not just the university area.

2. Contract Length

Match the broadband contract to your expected rental period.

3. Upload Speed

Important for video calls, cloud storage, file uploads and some gaming/remote-access situations.

4. Cost Per Person

Divide the total monthly bill by the number of people actually sharing it.

5. Router & Wi-Fi

A fast Fibre plan cannot compensate for poor Wi-Fi coverage.

6. QoS

For a busy shared house, traffic management can matter more than simply upgrading to a faster package.


NetBijak's Take

For students sharing a house, do not choose broadband by download speed alone.

The better decision process is:

Check Fibre Coverage → Check Contract Length → Compare Upload Speed → Calculate Cost Per Person → Check Router/Wi-Fi → Configure QoS

If you are renting for one academic year, a 12-month student Fibre plan can be particularly attractive because it reduces the mismatch between your rental period and broadband contract.

If TIME is available, its current Student Plans are worth checking first. If it is unavailable, Unifi and Maxis remain practical alternatives depending on the exact address, contract and any eligible bundle discounts.

For an 8-person house, spending a little more on the right plan and configuring QoS can be more useful than simply buying the highest advertised speed.

🎯Find My Plan →

title: Broadband Terbaik untuk CCTV Rumah dan Remote Monitoring di Malaysia
content:
Jika anda memasang CCTV di rumah di Malaysia, Upload Speed lebih penting daripada Download Speed apabila anda mahu melihat kamera dari luar rumah. Pelan Fibre 500Mbps biasanya sudah mencukupi untuk kebanyakan sistem CCTV rumah, tetapi keperluan sebenar bergantung pada Camera Bitrate, jumlah kamera yang dilihat serentak dan sama ada anda menggunakan Main Stream, Sub-stream atau P2P/Cloud.

Berapa Upload Bandwidth yang Diperlukan oleh CCTV 4K?

Tiada satu angka tetap untuk semua kamera 4K. Bitrate sebenar bergantung pada Resolution, Frame Rate, Compression, perubahan dalam scene dan tetapan kamera. Secara umum, Resolution dan Frame Rate yang lebih tinggi memerlukan lebih banyak bandwidth, manakala Compression yang lebih tinggi boleh mengurangkan Bitrate tetapi mungkin menjejaskan kualiti imej.

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

Untuk sistem CCTV rumah, anda boleh menggunakan angka berikut sebagai contoh perancangan:

Stream TypeContoh Bitrate Setiap KameraJumlah 4 KameraKegunaan Utama
Main Stream5–6Mbps20–24MbpsRakaman NVR berkualiti tinggi
Sub-streamSekitar 1MbpsSekitar 4MbpsRemote viewing melalui telefon

Angka ini hanyalah contoh untuk perancangan, bukan spesifikasi tetap bagi semua kamera 4K. Bitrate sebenar perlu diperiksa pada tetapan Camera / NVR anda.

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

Apa Maksudnya untuk Pengguna Fibre di Malaysia?

Di sinilah Upload Speed pelan Broadband anda menjadi penting.

Ramai pengguna di Malaysia memilih Fibre berdasarkan Download Speed seperti 300Mbps, 500Mbps atau 1Gbps. Tetapi apabila anda melihat CCTV dari luar rumah, video perlu dihantar keluar dari rumah melalui Upload Connection.

Sebagai contoh, pelan Unifi 300Mbps Home pada masa ini menawarkan sehingga 50Mbps Upload, manakala pelan 500Mbps menawarkan sehingga 100Mbps Upload. Jadi angka “500Mbps” tidak bermaksud Download dan Upload kedua-duanya 500Mbps.

(Source: Unifi — General FAQ / Unifi Home Package)

Upload Profile juga berbeza mengikut Fibre Provider. TIME, sebagai contoh, kini menawarkan 200Mbps Upload untuk pelan 200Mbps tertentu, manakala pelan 600Mbps dan 1Gbps menawarkan sehingga 500Mbps Upload.

(Source: TIME — Our Fibre Network)

Jadi, apabila memilih Broadband untuk CCTV di Malaysia, jangan bandingkan Download Speed sahaja. Semak Upload Speed juga.

Adakah CCTV 4K Sentiasa Menggunakan Internet Upload?

Tidak.

Jika kamera anda dirakam ke NVR di dalam rumah, laluan rakaman biasanya ialah:

Camera → Local Switch / LAN → NVR → Hard Drive

Ini bermaksud Main Stream boleh dirakam terus ke NVR melalui Local Network tanpa menghantar keseluruhan video 4K melalui Internet.

Internet Upload digunakan terutamanya apabila anda:

  1. Membuka CCTV App dari luar rumah
  2. Melihat Live View dari jauh
  3. Membuat Remote Playback
  4. Menggunakan Cloud Recording
  5. Menggunakan Cloud-based Monitoring Service

Jadi, sistem empat kamera masih boleh merakam video berkualiti tinggi ke NVR secara berterusan tanpa menggunakan banyak Internet Upload apabila tiada Remote Viewing.

Main Stream vs Sub-stream: Cara Kurangkan Penggunaan Upload

Kebanyakan IP Camera moden menyokong lebih daripada satu Video Stream.

Main Stream

Biasanya menggunakan Resolution dan Bitrate yang lebih tinggi. Ia lazimnya digunakan untuk Local NVR Recording atau Playback berkualiti tinggi.

Sub-stream

Menggunakan Resolution dan Bitrate yang lebih rendah. Ia sering digunakan untuk Mobile Remote Viewing kerana penggunaan Upload Bandwidth lebih rendah.

Contohnya, untuk empat kamera:

Jika setiap kamera menggunakan 5Mbps Main Stream:

4 × 5Mbps = 20Mbps

Jika aplikasi menggunakan Sub-stream sekitar 1Mbps setiap kamera:

4 × 1Mbps = 4Mbps

Formula mudah untuk perancangan:

CCTV Upload Requirement ≈ Jumlah Bitrate Remote Stream Serentak + Headroom

Jika sistem anda memerlukan kira-kira 20Mbps untuk Remote Viewing, menyediakan sekitar 25–30Mbps usable Upload Capacity memberikan lebih banyak ruang berbanding menggunakan connection pada had maksimum.

Broadband Berapa Laju yang Sesuai untuk CCTV Rumah di Malaysia?

Untuk CCTV rumah, anda tidak semestinya perlu terus membeli pelan 500Mbps atau 1Gbps.

Perkara pertama yang perlu dilihat ialah Upload Speed.

Setup CCTV asas

Jika sistem anda menggunakan:

  1. Local NVR Recording
  2. Sub-stream untuk Remote Viewing
  3. 2–4 kamera
  4. Remote Viewing sekali-sekala

Fibre dengan sekitar 30–50Mbps usable Upload biasanya sudah boleh digunakan, bergantung kepada Camera Bitrate.

Remote Monitoring yang lebih berat

Jika anda kerap:

  1. Melihat beberapa kamera 4K serentak
  2. Membenarkan beberapa pengguna mengakses CCTV
  3. Menggunakan Main Stream dengan Bitrate tinggi
  4. Membuat Remote Playback

Maka 50–100Mbps atau lebih Upload memberikan lebih banyak Headroom.

Maksudnya, jangan pilih Broadband hanya berdasarkan Download Speed. Padankan pelan dengan Bitrate sebenar sistem CCTV anda.

Adakah CCTV Remote Access Memerlukan Static IP?

Tidak semestinya.

Static IP boleh memudahkan sesetengah setup, tetapi ia bukan keperluan untuk semua sistem CCTV moden.

Tiga perkara utama yang perlu difahami ialah:

  1. Public IPv4 — Router boleh dicapai dari Internet.
  2. DDNS — Menyambungkan Hostname kepada Public IP yang berubah.
  3. CGNAT — ISP berkongsi satu lapisan NAT untuk ramai pengguna, yang biasanya menghalang Inbound Port Forwarding biasa.

Jika ISP memberikan Public IPv4 yang berubah-ubah, DDNS boleh digunakan untuk mengekalkan Hostname yang sama.

Contohnya:

cctv.example.com → Public IP Semasa Anda

Tetapi:

DDNS + CGNAT ≠ Direct Remote Access

DDNS hanya mengemaskini alamat IP. Ia tidak boleh mengatasi CGNAT pada rangkaian ISP.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

DDNS + Port Forwarding vs Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

CiriDDNS + Port ForwardingManufacturer P2P / Cloud
Tahap SetupLebih kompleksLebih mudah
Perlukan Public IPv4Biasanya yaSelalunya tidak
CGNATTidak sesuai untuk Inbound Forwarding biasaBanyak servis tidak memerlukan Inbound Port
Port ForwardingYaBiasanya tidak
Sesuai untukAdvanced usersKebanyakan pengguna rumah

Manufacturer P2P Service menggunakan pendekatan yang berbeza daripada DDNS + Port Forwarding. Banyak servis P2P direka supaya pengguna tidak perlu membuka Inbound Port secara manual, dan sesetengahnya boleh berfungsi di belakang CGNAT. Namun, cara ia berfungsi bergantung kepada vendor dan architecture servis tersebut.

(Source: Hikvision — Hik-Connect Remote Access Specifications)

Cara Setup CCTV Remote Access di Rumah

Step 1: Semak Camera Bitrate

Periksa tetapan Camera atau NVR:

  1. Resolution
  2. Frame Rate
  3. Main Stream Bitrate
  4. Sub-stream Bitrate
  5. Jumlah kamera

Jangan menganggarkan penggunaan bandwidth hanya berdasarkan label “4K”.

Step 2: Uji Actual Upload Speed

Gunakan sambungan wired jika boleh semasa membuat Speed Test.

Jika pelan anda diiklankan dengan 50Mbps Upload tetapi actual speed jauh lebih rendah, Upload Headroom untuk CCTV juga akan berkurang.

Step 3: Semak Sama Ada Anda Mempunyai Public IPv4

Bandingkan WAN IP yang ditunjukkan pada Router dengan Public IP yang dilihat dari Internet.

Jika kedua-duanya berbeza, ini menunjukkan Router anda berada di belakang satu lagi NAT layer. CGNAT ialah salah satu kemungkinan.

Jika WAN IP Router berada dalam julat 100.64.0.0/10, ia merupakan petunjuk kuat bahawa anda berada di belakang CGNAT.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

Step 4: Pilih Remote Access Method

Jika anda mempunyai Public IPv4 dan faham konfigurasi rangkaian:

DDNS + Port Forwarding

Jika ISP anda menggunakan CGNAT atau anda mahu setup yang lebih mudah:

Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

Untuk pengguna advanced yang mahu kawalan lebih baik terhadap remote access:

VPN-based Remote Access

Adakah CCTV Port Forwarding Selamat?

Port Forwarding tidak semestinya tidak selamat, tetapi ia menyebabkan service tertentu boleh terdedah kepada Public Internet.

Jika anda menggunakannya:

  1. Buka hanya Port yang benar-benar diperlukan.
  2. Pastikan Firmware NVR / Camera sentiasa dikemas kini.
  3. Gunakan password yang kuat dan unik.
  4. Jangan dedahkan management service yang tidak diperlukan.
  5. Gunakan HTTPS / encrypted connection jika disokong.
  6. Pertimbangkan VPN untuk setup yang lebih terkawal.

Panduan keselamatan Hikvision juga mengesyorkan supaya Internet-exposed ports diminimumkan dan Port Forwarding hanya digunakan apabila perlu.

(Source: Hikvision — Network Camera Security Guide)

Bagaimana dengan 4G atau 5G sebagai Backup?

Boleh.

4G/5G Backup boleh mengekalkan sambungan Internet apabila Fibre utama mengalami gangguan.

Namun, Mobile Broadband kerap menggunakan Private IP atau CGNAT. Ini bermakna traditional Inbound Port Forwarding mungkin tidak boleh digunakan.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

Sebab itu, untuk CCTV yang perlu kekal boleh diakses melalui 4G/5G Backup, Manufacturer P2P / Cloud biasanya lebih praktikal berbanding Port Forwarding biasa.


NetBijak's Take

Untuk CCTV rumah di Malaysia, jangan pilih Broadband berdasarkan Download Speed sahaja.

Setup yang lebih praktikal ialah:

4K Cameras → Local NVR (Main Stream) → Sub-stream untuk Mobile Viewing → Home Fibre → P2P/Cloud atau DDNS

Sebelum anda upgrade daripada 300Mbps kepada 500Mbps atau 1Gbps, semak dahulu Upload Speed, Camera Bitrate dan Remote Access Method.

Sebagai contoh, Unifi 300Mbps kini menawarkan sehingga 50Mbps Upload, manakala 500Mbps menawarkan sehingga 100Mbps. TIME pula mempunyai beberapa pelan Fibre rumah dengan Upload Speed yang jauh lebih tinggi.

(Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Package; TIME — Our Fibre Network)

Broadband terbaik untuk CCTV bukan semestinya pelan dengan Download Speed paling tinggi. Yang lebih penting ialah Upload Headroom yang mencukupi dan Remote Access Method yang sesuai dengan rangkaian ISP anda.

title: 马来西亚家庭 CCTV 远程监控宽带怎么选？
content:
如果你在马来西亚安装家庭 CCTV，真正影响远程监控体验的往往不是 Download Speed，而是 Upload Speed。500Mbps 的 Fibre 对大多数家庭 CCTV 已经绰绰有余，但实际需求取决于摄像头 Bitrate、同时观看的摄像头数量，以及你使用 Main Stream、Sub-stream 还是 P2P/Cloud。

4K CCTV 摄像头需要多少 Upload Bandwidth？

4K 摄像头没有一个固定的带宽需求。实际 Bitrate 会受到 Resolution、Frame Rate、Compression、场景变化以及摄像头设置影响。一般来说，Resolution 和 Frame Rate 越高，需要的带宽越多；提高 Compression 可以降低 Bitrate，但可能影响画质。

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

以家庭 CCTV 为例，可以先用以下数字做规划：

Stream Type单摄像头示例 Bitrate4 台摄像头总计主要用途
Main Stream5–6Mbps20–24Mbps高画质本地录像
Sub-stream约 1Mbps约 4Mbps手机远程查看

这些只是规划参考值，并不是所有 4K 摄像头的固定规格。实际 Bitrate 需要根据你的 Camera / NVR 设置确认。

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

这对马来西亚 Fibre 用户意味着什么？

这里就涉及 Broadband Plan 的 Upload Speed。

马来西亚很多消费者选择 Fibre 时，首先看的是 300Mbps、500Mbps 或 1Gbps 的 Download Speed。但 CCTV 远程观看使用的是从你家上传到 Internet 的带宽。

例如，TM Unifi 目前的 300Mbps Home Plan 提供最高 50Mbps Upload，500Mbps Plan 则提供最高 100Mbps Upload。所以“500Mbps”并不代表 Download 和 Upload 都是 500Mbps，CCTV 用户需要单独查看 Upload 规格。

(Source: Unifi — General FAQ / Unifi Home Package)

不同 Fibre Provider 的 Upload Profile 也可能差很多。例如，TIME 目前的 200Mbps Home Plan 提供 200Mbps Upload，而 600Mbps 和 1Gbps Home Plan 则提供 500Mbps Upload。

(Source: TIME — Our Fibre Network)

因此，在马来西亚选择 CCTV 宽带时，不要只比较 Download Speed，也要比较 Upload Speed。

4K CCTV 是否一直占用你的 Internet Upload？

不是。

如果摄像头连接到本地 NVR，正常的录像路径是：

Camera → Local Switch / LAN → NVR → Hard Drive

因此，Main Stream 可以在家里的 Local Network 内直接录入 NVR，不需要把完整的 4K 视频持续上传到 Internet。

Internet Upload 主要会在以下情况使用：

  1. 在外面打开 CCTV App
  2. 远程观看 Live View
  3. 远程 Playback
  4. 使用 Cloud Recording
  5. 使用 Cloud-based Monitoring Service

所以，4 台摄像头可以持续以高画质录制到本地 NVR，而在没有人远程查看时，Internet Upload 使用量相对较低。

Main Stream vs Sub-stream：降低远程监控带宽的关键

大多数现代 IP Camera 都支持多个 Video Stream。

Main Stream

通常使用较高 Resolution 和 Bitrate，主要用于本地 NVR 录像或高画质 Playback。

Sub-stream

使用较低 Resolution 和 Bitrate，通常用于手机远程查看，因为它需要的 Upload Bandwidth 更少。

例如 4 台摄像头：

如果每台远程传输 5Mbps Main Stream：

4 × 5Mbps = 20Mbps

如果 App 使用每台约 1Mbps 的 Sub-stream：

4 × 1Mbps = 4Mbps

实际规划时可以使用：

CCTV Upload Requirement ≈ 同时远程观看的总 Bitrate + Headroom

例如需要约 20Mbps 的远程视频流，实际最好准备约 25–30Mbps 可用 Upload Capacity，不要让 CCTV 长时间把线路跑到极限。

马来西亚家庭 CCTV 需要多快的宽带？

对于家庭 CCTV，重点不是一定要购买 500Mbps 或 1Gbps。

首先看 Upload Speed。

基本 CCTV 使用

如果你的系统主要是：

  1. Local NVR Recording
  2. Sub-stream Remote Viewing
  3. 2–4 台摄像头
  4. 偶尔通过手机查看

那么拥有约 30–50Mbps 可用 Upload 的 Fibre Plan 通常已经可以满足实际需求，具体仍取决于 Camera Bitrate。

经常远程查看高画质画面

如果你经常需要：

  1. 同时查看多台 4K Camera
  2. 多人同时远程查看
  3. 使用高 Bitrate Main Stream
  4. 远程 Playback

那么 50–100Mbps 或更高 Upload 会提供更多 Headroom。

关键不是单纯购买更快的 Download，而是根据 CCTV 实际 Bitrate 来选择 Broadband。

CCTV 远程访问需要 Static IP 吗？

不一定。

Static IP 有帮助，但不是现代家庭 CCTV 的必需品。

这里需要理解三个概念：

  1. Public IPv4 — Router 可以从 Internet 被访问。
  2. DDNS — 将不断变化的 Public IP 对应到固定 Hostname。
  3. CGNAT — ISP 在网络层将多个用户放在共享 NAT 后面，通常无法进行正常的 Inbound Port Forwarding。

如果 ISP 提供的是动态但可以从 Internet 访问的 Public IPv4，就可以使用 DDNS。

例如：

cctv.example.com → 你的当前 Public IP

但：

DDNS + CGNAT ≠ Direct Remote Access

DDNS 可以告诉你当前 Public IP 是什么，却无法绕过 ISP 层面的 CGNAT。

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

DDNS + Port Forwarding vs Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

功能DDNS + Port ForwardingManufacturer P2P / Cloud
设置难度较高较低
需要 Public IPv4通常需要通常不需要
CGNAT不适合传统 Inbound Forwarding很多方案无需 Inbound Port
Port Forwarding需要通常不需要
适合用户进阶用户大多数家庭用户

Manufacturer P2P Service 与传统 DDNS + Port Forwarding 的工作方式不同。很多 P2P 服务不需要用户直接开放 Inbound Port，因此在 CGNAT 环境下也可能正常工作，但具体行为取决于 CCTV 厂商及其服务架构。

(Source: Hikvision — Hik-Connect Remote Access Specifications)

马来西亚家庭 CCTV 怎么设置远程访问？

Step 1：检查 Camera Bitrate

进入 Camera 或 NVR 设置，确认：

  1. Resolution
  2. Frame Rate
  3. Main Stream Bitrate
  4. Sub-stream Bitrate
  5. Camera 数量

不要只看到“4K”就估算带宽。

Step 2：测试实际 Upload Speed

尽可能使用有线连接进行 Speed Test。

如果 Broadband Plan 标称 50Mbps Upload，但实际测速明显低于这个水平，那么 CCTV 可以使用的 Upload Headroom 也会减少。

Step 3：确认是否拥有 Public IPv4

比较 Router 显示的 WAN IP 与外部 IP Check Service 显示的 Public IP。

如果两者不同，说明 Router 后面还有另一层 NAT。CGNAT 是其中一种可能性。

如果 Router WAN IP 落在 100.64.0.0/10 范围内，则是判断 CGNAT 的一个强烈信号。

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

Step 4：选择 Remote Access 方式

如果你拥有 Public IPv4，并且熟悉网络设置：

DDNS + Port Forwarding

如果 ISP 使用 CGNAT，或者希望简单一点：

Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

如果你希望进一步控制暴露在 Internet 上的服务：

VPN-based Remote Access

CCTV Port Forwarding 安全吗？

Port Forwarding 本身并不代表一定不安全，但它会让指定服务直接暴露到 Public Internet。

如果必须使用：

  1. 只开放真正需要的 Port
  2. 保持 NVR / Camera Firmware 更新
  3. 使用强密码和独立密码
  4. 不要暴露不必要的管理服务
  5. 能使用 HTTPS / 加密连接时优先使用
  6. 进阶用户可以考虑 VPN

Hikvision 的安全指南同样建议减少暴露在 Internet 上的 Port，并只在必要时使用 Port Forwarding。

(Source: Hikvision — Network Camera Security Guide)

4G / 5G 可以作为 CCTV Backup 吗？

可以。

4G/5G Backup 可以在主要 Fibre 断线时继续提供 Internet Connectivity，让远程 CCTV 保持在线。

但 Mobile Broadband 经常使用 Private IP 或 CGNAT，因此传统 Inbound Port Forwarding 可能无法正常工作。

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

因此，如果 CCTV 需要通过 4G/5G Backup 保持远程访问，Manufacturer P2P / Cloud 通常会比传统 Port Forwarding 更实际。


NetBijak's Take

对于马来西亚家庭 CCTV，不要只看 Broadband 的 Download Speed。

更合理的架构是：

4K Cameras → Local NVR（Main Stream）→ Sub-stream 手机查看 → Home Fibre → P2P/Cloud 或 DDNS

在从 300Mbps 升级到 500Mbps 或 1Gbps 之前，先检查你的 Upload Speed、Camera Bitrate 和 Remote Access Method。

例如 Unifi 目前 300Mbps Home Plan 的 Upload 最高为 50Mbps，500Mbps 则为 100Mbps；TIME 的部分 Home Fibre Plan 则提供明显更高的 Upload Speed。

(Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Package; TIME — Our Fibre Network)

对于 CCTV 来说，最好的 Broadband Plan 不一定是 Download Speed 最大的那个，而是能够提供足够 Upload Headroom，并且能够配合你的 ISP 网络架构正常进行 Remote Access 的方案。

title: Best Broadband for Home CCTV Remote Monitoring in Malaysia
content:
If you are installing CCTV at home in Malaysia, upload speed matters more than the headline download speed when you want to watch your cameras remotely. A 500Mbps fibre plan can be more than enough for CCTV, but the actual requirement depends on camera bitrate, how many cameras are viewed simultaneously, and whether you use Main Stream, Sub-stream or cloud/P2P access.

How Much Upload Bandwidth Does a 4K CCTV Camera Need?

There is no single fixed bandwidth requirement for a 4K camera. The actual bitrate depends on resolution, frame rate, compression, scene activity and camera settings. Higher resolution and frame rate generally require more bandwidth, while stronger compression can reduce bitrate at the expense of image quality.

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

For planning purposes, a typical home CCTV system might look like this:

Stream TypeExample Per-Camera Bitrate4-Camera TotalPrimary Use
Main Stream5–6Mbps20–24MbpsHigh-quality recording
Sub-stream~1Mbps~4MbpsRemote mobile viewing

These are planning examples, not fixed camera specifications. Your actual bitrate can be significantly different depending on the camera model and configuration.

(Source: Axis — AXIS OS Web Interface Help)

What Does This Mean for Malaysian Fibre Users?

This is where your broadband plan's upload speed becomes important.

Many Malaysian users choose fibre based on the advertised download speed, such as 300Mbps, 500Mbps or 1Gbps. But CCTV remote viewing uses the upload path from your home to the Internet.

For example, TM Unifi currently lists its 300Mbps Home plan with up to 50Mbps upload, while its 500Mbps plan provides up to 100Mbps upload. This means a 500Mbps plan does not simply provide “500Mbps for everything” — the upload side is a separate specification that matters for remote CCTV. (Source: Unifi — General FAQ / Unifi Home Package)

Other Malaysian fibre providers can have very different upload profiles. TIME, for example, currently lists 200Mbps with 200Mbps upload, while its 600Mbps and 1Gbps home plans offer 500Mbps upload. (Source: TIME — Our Fibre Network)

So when choosing broadband for CCTV in Malaysia, compare the upload speed — not just the download number on the plan.

Does 4K CCTV Always Use Your Internet Upload?

No.

If your cameras are recording to a local NVR, the normal recording path is:

Camera → Local Switch / LAN → NVR → Hard Drive

The Main Stream can therefore be recorded locally without sending the entire 4K video stream over the Internet.

Internet upload becomes important when someone:

  1. Opens the CCTV app remotely
  2. Watches live footage outside the home
  3. Plays back footage remotely
  4. Uses cloud recording or cloud-based services
  5. Connects through a remote monitoring platform

A four-camera system can therefore record high-quality footage locally while using relatively little Internet upload when nobody is remotely viewing the cameras.

Main Stream vs Sub-stream: The Key to Lower Upload Usage

Most modern IP cameras support multiple video streams.

Main Stream

Usually configured for higher resolution and bitrate. It is typically used for local NVR recording or high-quality playback.

Sub-stream

Uses a lower resolution and bitrate. It is commonly used for mobile remote viewing because it reduces bandwidth consumption.

This distinction can make a major difference.

If four cameras each transmit a 5Mbps Main Stream remotely:

4 × 5Mbps = 20Mbps

If the app instead uses a 1Mbps Sub-stream:

4 × 1Mbps = 4Mbps

A practical planning formula is:

CCTV Upload Requirement ≈ Total Bitrate of Simultaneous Remote Streams + Headroom

For example, a 20Mbps remote stream load would be more comfortable with around 25–30Mbps of usable upload capacity, rather than operating continuously at the connection limit.

What Broadband Speed Is Enough for Home CCTV in Malaysia?

For most home installations, the key question is not whether you need 500Mbps or 1Gbps download.

Look at the upload side.

Basic CCTV setup

If you mainly use:

  1. Local NVR recording
  2. Sub-stream for remote viewing
  3. 2–4 cameras
  4. Occasional mobile access

A fibre plan with around 30–50Mbps usable upload can already be workable, depending on the camera bitrate.

Higher-quality remote monitoring

If you regularly monitor:

  1. Multiple 4K cameras
  2. Several cameras simultaneously
  3. High-bitrate Main Streams
  4. Remote playback

Then having 50–100Mbps or more upload gives you substantially more headroom.

The important point is that the camera system should be designed around its actual bitrate rather than simply buying the fastest download plan available.

Do You Need a Static IP for Remote CCTV?

No.

A Static IP is useful, but it is not mandatory.

There are three concepts you need to understand:

  1. Public IPv4 — your router can be reached from the Internet.
  2. DDNS — gives your changing public IP a fixed hostname.
  3. CGNAT — puts multiple customers behind an ISP-level NAT, preventing normal inbound port forwarding.

If your ISP provides a changing but publicly reachable IPv4 address, DDNS can keep your CCTV hostname updated.

For example:

cctv.example.com → Your Current Public IP

However:

DDNS + CGNAT ≠ Direct Remote Access

DDNS can tell you what your public IP is. It cannot create inbound connectivity through an ISP-level CGNAT system.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

DDNS + Port Forwarding vs Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

FeatureDDNS + Port ForwardingManufacturer P2P / Cloud
Setup ComplexityHigherLower
Public IPv4 NeededUsually yesOften no
CGNATNot suitable for normal inbound forwardingOften designed to work without inbound forwarding
Port ForwardingRequiredUsually not
Best ForAdvanced usersMost residential users

Manufacturer P2P services are designed differently from traditional DDNS + port forwarding. Many can establish remote connectivity without requiring you to expose the NVR directly through an inbound port, although the exact architecture depends on the manufacturer and service.

(Source: Hikvision — Hik-Connect Remote Access Specifications)

How to Set Up Home CCTV Remote Access

Step 1: Check Your Camera Bitrate

Open the camera or NVR settings and check:

  1. Resolution
  2. Frame rate
  3. Main Stream bitrate
  4. Sub-stream bitrate
  5. Number of cameras

Do not estimate bandwidth based only on the “4K” label.

Step 2: Test Your Actual Upload Speed

Run a speed test using a wired connection where possible.

If your broadband package advertises 50Mbps upload but your actual connection only delivers significantly less, your available CCTV headroom will also be lower.

Step 3: Check Whether You Have a Public IPv4

Compare the WAN IP shown on your router with the public IP shown by an external IP-check service.

If they differ, your router is behind another NAT layer. CGNAT is one possible explanation.

If the router WAN address falls within the 100.64.0.0/10 range, that is a strong indication of CGNAT.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

Step 4: Choose the Right Remote Access Method

If you have a public IPv4 and understand networking:

DDNS + Port Forwarding

If your ISP uses CGNAT or you want a simpler setup:

Manufacturer P2P / Cloud

For advanced users who want tighter control over exposed services:

VPN-based remote access

Is CCTV Port Forwarding Safe?

Port forwarding is not automatically unsafe, but it increases your exposure to the public Internet.

If you use it:

  1. Forward only the ports actually required.
  2. Keep the NVR/camera firmware updated.
  3. Use strong, unique passwords.
  4. Avoid exposing unnecessary management services.
  5. Prefer encrypted access where supported.
  6. Consider VPN access instead of directly exposing the NVR.

Hikvision's own security guidance recommends minimising Internet-exposed ports and configuring port forwarding only when necessary.

(Source: Hikvision — Network Camera Security Guide)

What About 4G or 5G Backup?

A 4G/5G backup connection can keep remote CCTV accessible when your primary fibre connection fails.

However, mobile broadband frequently uses private or CGNAT addressing, which can make traditional inbound port forwarding difficult or impossible.

(Source: TP-Link — Port Forwarding and CGNAT Troubleshooting)

For this reason, manufacturer P2P/Cloud access is often the more practical option when CCTV needs to remain remotely accessible over a 4G/5G backup connection.


NetBijak's Take

For Malaysian homes, do not choose a broadband plan for CCTV based on download speed alone.

A better setup is:

4K Cameras → Local NVR (Main Stream) → Sub-stream for Mobile Viewing → Home Fibre → P2P/Cloud or DDNS

Before upgrading from 300Mbps to 500Mbps or 1Gbps, first check your ISP's actual upload speed, camera bitrate and remote viewing method.

For example, Unifi's current 300Mbps plan provides up to 50Mbps upload, while its 500Mbps plan provides up to 100Mbps. TIME's current residential plans can offer substantially higher upload speeds at comparable tiers. That difference can matter more to a multi-camera CCTV installation than another few hundred Mbps of download capacity. (Source: Unifi — Unifi Home Package; TIME — Our Fibre Network)

The right CCTV broadband plan is not the one with the biggest download number. It is the one that gives your cameras enough upload headroom and a remote-access architecture that actually works with your ISP's network.

title: Pembaikan Kabel Dasar Laut: Kenapa Website Antarabangsa Tiba-Tiba Jadi Slow?
content:
Kalau website Malaysia masih boleh dibuka seperti biasa tetapi website dari Amerika Syarikat, Jepun atau negara lain tiba-tiba menjadi sangat slow, masalah itu tidak semestinya datang daripada Fibre Broadband di rumah anda.

Apabila kabel dasar laut antarabangsa mengalami kerosakan atau menjalani maintenance, kapasiti untuk membawa trafik antara Malaysia dan rangkaian luar negara boleh berkurang. ISP kemudian akan mengalihkan trafik melalui laluan lain, tetapi laluan alternatif mungkin lebih jauh atau lebih sesak.

Sebab itu Internet masih boleh digunakan, tetapi prestasi untuk sesetengah website antarabangsa boleh jatuh dengan ketara.

Kenapa Malaysia Bergantung Pada Kabel Dasar Laut?

Sambungan Fibre di rumah anda bukanlah sambungan terus ke semua server di seluruh dunia.

Apabila anda membuka website yang servernya berada di luar negara, trafik biasanya bergerak melalui rangkaian ISP tempatan sebelum masuk ke rangkaian antarabangsa dan seterusnya melalui satu atau lebih sistem kabel dasar laut.

Secara ringkas, laluan itu boleh kelihatan seperti:

Rumah → Rangkaian ISP → International Gateway → Kabel Dasar Laut → Rangkaian Luar Negara → Server

Kalau anda membuka website yang servernya berada di Malaysia, trafik mungkin kekal dalam rangkaian domestik untuk sebahagian besar laluannya.

Tetapi kalau server berada di Amerika Syarikat, Jepun atau Eropah, trafik perlu melalui sambungan antarabangsa.

Sebab itu keadaan seperti ini boleh berlaku:

Website Malaysia normal, website luar negara slow.

Ia tidak semestinya bermaksud Fibre di rumah anda bermasalah.

Apa Berlaku Bila Kabel Dasar Laut Rosak?

Kerosakan satu kabel tidak semestinya menyebabkan seluruh Internet terputus.

Masalah yang lebih biasa ialah kapasiti pada laluan antarabangsa tertentu berkurang.

ISP dan network operator yang besar biasanya mempunyai lebih daripada satu sambungan antarabangsa. Apabila satu kabel mengalami gangguan, trafik boleh dialihkan ke laluan lain yang masih tersedia.

Proses ini biasanya dipanggil rerouting.

Contohnya, sebelum gangguan:

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable A → Overseas Transit → Server

Selepas Cable A bermasalah:

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable B → Overseas Transit → Server

Sambungan masih boleh berfungsi, tetapi Cable B mungkin mempunyai laluan yang lebih panjang atau kapasiti yang lebih terhad.

Jadi:

Cable rosak tidak semestinya bermaksud Internet terus terputus.

Tetapi:

Rerouting juga tidak bermaksud prestasi akan kekal sama seperti sebelum gangguan.

APCN2 dan AAG: Contoh Gangguan Yang Pernah Memberi Kesan Kepada Malaysia

Malaysia pernah berdepan gangguan yang melibatkan sistem kabel dasar laut antarabangsa seperti APCN2 dan AAG.

APCN2

Asia Pacific Cable Network 2 (APCN2) ialah sistem kabel dasar laut yang menghubungkan beberapa pasaran telekomunikasi utama di Asia.

Semasa gangguan APCN2 sebelum ini, TM melaporkan bahawa kapasiti antarabangsa mereka terjejas tetapi trafik boleh dialihkan dan dioptimumkan melalui laluan antarabangsa alternatif.

Ini menunjukkan kenapa kerosakan satu kabel tidak semestinya menyebabkan pengguna Malaysia kehilangan sambungan Internet sepenuhnya.

Trafik masih boleh bergerak melalui laluan lain.

Masalah seterusnya ialah sama ada laluan alternatif tersebut mempunyai kapasiti yang mencukupi.

Bagaimana Dengan AAG?

Asia-America Gateway (AAG) ialah sistem kabel dasar laut yang menghubungkan Asia Tenggara dengan destinasi antarabangsa termasuk Amerika Syarikat dan Hong Kong.

Semasa maintenance AAG sebelum ini, TM memberi amaran bahawa sesetengah perkhidmatan yang bergantung kepada laluan tersebut mungkin mengalami degradation. TM juga menyatakan trafik akan dialihkan ke laluan alternatif untuk mengurangkan kesan kepada pengguna.

Sebab itu pengumuman cable maintenance biasanya tidak bermaksud:

“Semua Internet di Malaysia akan slow.”

Kesan sebenar bergantung kepada laluan mana yang terjejas dan ke mana trafik pengguna tersebut perlu pergi.

Bagaimana Sebenarnya ISP Buat Rerouting?

Rerouting bukan sekadar “tukar kepada kabel lain”.

Internet terdiri daripada ribuan rangkaian yang saling berhubung dan rangkaian ini bertukar maklumat tentang laluan yang boleh digunakan.

Di peringkat Internet yang lebih besar, salah satu mekanisme utama ialah BGP (Border Gateway Protocol).

BGP digunakan untuk mengiklankan IP Prefix yang boleh dicapai melalui sesuatu rangkaian dan laluan yang tersedia untuk sampai ke destinasi tersebut.

Apabila sesuatu laluan tidak lagi tersedia atau network operator perlu mengubah trafik, maklumat routing boleh berubah dan trafik boleh dihantar melalui laluan alternatif.

Bagi pengguna biasa, cara paling mudah untuk memahami proses ini ialah:

Destinasi sama, tetapi laluan untuk sampai ke destinasi sudah berubah.

Perubahan laluan ini boleh memberi kesan kepada tiga perkara utama.

Latency

Laluan baharu mungkin lebih jauh atau melalui lebih banyak network hops, menyebabkan ping meningkat.

Packet Loss

Jika trafik yang banyak dialihkan ke laluan yang mempunyai kapasiti terhad, congestion boleh menyebabkan packet loss.

Throughput

Apabila sambungan TCP mengesan packet loss atau congestion, ia akan mengurangkan kadar penghantaran.

Sebab itu anda boleh mempunyai Fibre 500Mbps atau 1Gbps, tetapi download daripada server luar negara masih sangat perlahan.

Masalah mungkin bukan pada kelajuan Fibre anda, tetapi pada laluan antarabangsa menuju server tersebut.

Kenapa Internet Masih Boleh Jadi Slow Selepas Rerouting?

Bayangkan laluan asal mempunyai banyak kapasiti yang masih kosong.

Apabila satu kabel mengalami gangguan, trafik yang biasanya melalui kabel tersebut perlu diserap oleh laluan lain.

Kalau kapasiti alternatif mencukupi, kebanyakan pengguna mungkin tidak perasan banyak perbezaan.

Tetapi kalau terlalu banyak trafik dipindahkan ke laluan yang sama, congestion boleh berlaku.

Sebab itu prestasi juga boleh berubah mengikut masa.

Contohnya:

3 pagi → website US normal

9 malam → website US sangat slow

Pada waktu puncak, laluan antarabangsa alternatif mungkin sudah membawa trafik yang tinggi.

Anda juga mungkin melihat keadaan seperti:

  1. Website Singapore normal
  2. Website US slow
  3. Ping ke server Jepun meningkat
  4. Online gaming mengalami latency tinggi
  5. VPN menjadi tidak stabil
  6. Download dari server luar negara menjadi perlahan

Corak seperti ini lebih berguna untuk troubleshooting berbanding hanya melihat satu keputusan Speed Test.

Kenapa Hanya Website Tertentu Yang Slow?

Kerosakan kabel dasar laut tidak memberi kesan yang sama kepada semua website.

Website berbeza menggunakan laluan berbeza

Server di Singapore, Japan dan US mungkin menggunakan laluan antarabangsa yang berbeza.

Jadi, website Singapore yang normal tidak bermaksud laluan ke US juga normal.

Website mungkin menggunakan CDN

Platform besar biasanya menggunakan Content Delivery Network (CDN).

Content boleh disimpan di server yang lebih dekat dengan pengguna. Ini bermakna anda mungkin tidak perlu berhubung terus dengan Origin Server di US atau Eropah.

Sebab itu sesetengah platform masih boleh berfungsi dengan baik walaupun satu laluan antarabangsa mengalami gangguan.

ISP berbeza mempunyai international connectivity yang berbeza

Dua pengguna yang tinggal berdekatan tidak semestinya menggunakan laluan antarabangsa yang sama.

ISP A mungkin mempunyai laluan alternatif yang kurang sesak, manakala ISP B mungkin menggunakan laluan yang mengalami congestion.

Sebab itu:

“Kawan saya guna ISP lain dan tak ada masalah.”

tidak semestinya bermaksud Fibre anda rosak.

Kenapa Speed Test Masih Boleh Dapat 500Mbps?

Speed Test tidak mengukur “seluruh Internet”.

Ia mengukur sambungan antara peranti anda dengan server ujian tertentu.

Kalau server tersebut berada di Malaysia atau mempunyai peering yang baik dengan ISP anda, trafik ujian mungkin tidak melalui laluan antarabangsa yang sedang bermasalah.

Jadi anda boleh mendapat:

Speed Test Malaysia: 500Mbps

tetapi:

Download dari server US: sangat slow

Kedua-dua keputusan itu boleh menjadi betul kerana kedua-duanya menggunakan network path yang berbeza.

Untuk troubleshooting, bandingkan beberapa destinasi:

  1. Malaysia
  2. Singapore
  3. Hong Kong
  4. Japan
  5. United States

Kalau local connection masih normal tetapi beberapa destinasi antarabangsa menunjukkan latency atau packet loss yang lebih tinggi, international routing menjadi salah satu kemungkinan utama.

Nak Semak Laluan Dengan Lebih Terperinci? Gunakan Traceroute

Pengguna yang lebih teknikal boleh menggunakan Traceroute untuk melihat laluan trafik.

Untuk Windows:

tracert example.com

Untuk macOS atau Linux:

traceroute example.com

Traceroute menunjukkan network hops antara peranti anda dan destinasi.

Tetapi jangan terus membuat kesimpulan hanya kerana satu hop menunjukkan packet loss.

Sesetengah router memang tidak memberi respons kepada semua ICMP request. Jadi packet loss pada satu intermediate hop tidak semestinya bermaksud connection sebenar mengalami packet loss.

Apa yang lebih berguna ialah melihat corak keseluruhan laluan.

Contohnya:

Malaysia → ISP Network → International Gateway → Singapore → US → Destination

Kalau laluan ke destinasi tertentu tiba-tiba berubah atau latency meningkat dengan ketara selepas trafik meninggalkan rangkaian Malaysia, itu boleh menjadi petunjuk bahawa masalah berlaku pada bahagian antarabangsa.

Lebih baik buat perbandingan dengan destinasi lain dan pada waktu yang berbeza.

Kenapa Packet Loss Kadang-Kadang Lebih Teruk Daripada Speed Yang Rendah?

Ramai pengguna hanya melihat Mbps.

Untuk sambungan antarabangsa, latency dan packet loss juga sangat penting.

Apabila TCP mengesan packet loss, ia menganggap terdapat congestion atau masalah penghantaran dan akan mengurangkan kadar penghantaran.

Akibatnya, packet loss yang berterusan walaupun tidak terlalu tinggi boleh memberi kesan besar kepada sambungan jarak jauh.

Contohnya, Fibre anda masih mempunyai kapasiti ratusan Mbps di Malaysia, tetapi laluan ke server US mengalami congestion dan packet loss.

Hasilnya:

Local Fibre laju, tetapi download dari US tetap slow.

Kesan ini lebih mudah dirasai pada:

  1. Cloud Services
  2. International File Downloads
  3. Remote Desktop
  4. VPN
  5. Online Gaming
  6. Video Conferencing

Boleh Tukar ISP Untuk Selesaikan Masalah Kabel Dasar Laut?

Kadang-kadang boleh, tetapi bukan jaminan.

Perkara paling penting bukan jenama ISP, tetapi international connectivity yang digunakan oleh ISP tersebut.

Dua ISP yang berbeza mungkin menggunakan laluan antarabangsa yang berbeza.

Sebaliknya, dua perkhidmatan broadband yang kelihatan berbeza juga mungkin berkongsi upstream network, transit atau kapasiti tertentu.

Jadi kalau masalah berlaku pada international route, upgrade:

300Mbps → 500Mbps → 1Gbps

tidak semestinya menyelesaikan masalah.

Anda hanya menambah kapasiti Fibre antara rumah dengan ISP. Anda tidak secara automatik menambah kapasiti pada laluan antarabangsa yang sedang congestion.

Berapa Lama Kabel Dasar Laut Ambil Untuk Dibaiki?

Tiada satu tempoh standard.

Kerja membaiki kabel dasar laut memerlukan kapal dan peralatan khusus, dan tempohnya boleh bergantung kepada:

  1. Lokasi kerosakan
  2. Cuaca dan keadaan laut
  3. Availability repair vessel
  4. Akses kepada lokasi kerosakan
  5. Spare cable
  6. Jumlah cable segment yang terjejas
  7. Koordinasi antara cable owners dan operators

Tetapi ada satu perkara penting yang ramai pengguna terlepas pandang:

Physical repair time tidak sama dengan customer impact time.

ISP boleh memulihkan prestasi melalui rerouting sebelum kabel yang rosak selesai dibaiki.

Sebaliknya, kabel yang masih beroperasi tetapi mempunyai kapasiti terhad semasa maintenance juga boleh menyebabkan congestion.

Macam Mana Nak Tahu Masalah Datang Dari Fibre Rumah Atau International Network?

Jangan bergantung kepada satu Speed Test sahaja.

Kemungkinan masalahKemungkinan masalah
Website Malaysia dan luar negara semua slowWiFi, router, Fibre, access network atau ISP
Website Malaysia normal tetapi website luar negara tertentu slowInternational routing atau destination
Beberapa destinasi luar negara tiba-tiba latency tinggiInternational connectivity
Hanya satu website slowServer, CDN atau website tersebut juga mungkin bermasalah
ISP berbeza menunjukkan prestasi berbezaPerbezaan routing atau upstream
Speed Test normal tetapi download luar negara slowCongestion, packet loss atau server limitation

Ia bukan diagnosis muktamad, tetapi cukup untuk membantu anda menentukan arah troubleshooting.

Apa Patut Pengguna Malaysia Buat Bila Berlaku Cable Incident?

Kalau ISP sudah mengesahkan berlaku International Cable Fault atau Maintenance, dan local connection di rumah masih normal, tidak banyak manfaat untuk restart ONT atau router berulang kali.

Sebaliknya, periksa:

  1. Adakah website Malaysia normal?
  2. Website luar negara mana yang terjejas?
  3. Adakah negara tertentu sahaja yang bermasalah?
  4. Adakah latency meningkat?
  5. Adakah terdapat packet loss?
  6. Adakah ISP sudah mengeluarkan pengumuman mengenai international network incident?

Kalau perlu hubungi ISP, berikan maklumat yang spesifik:

  1. Website yang terjejas
  2. Masa masalah berlaku
  3. Negara destinasi
  4. Ping / latency
  5. Traceroute result

Maklumat ini jauh lebih berguna daripada hanya memberitahu customer service:

“Internet saya slow.”


NetBijak’s Take

Kabel dasar laut bermasalah tidak bermaksud Fibre rumah anda rosak.

Perkara paling penting ialah mengenal pasti di mana bottleneck berlaku — sama ada pada WiFi, Fibre access network, ISP atau international route menuju destinasi tertentu.

Kalau website Malaysia masih normal tetapi website luar negara tertentu tiba-tiba mengalami latency tinggi, packet loss atau throughput rendah, semak international routing sebelum menyalahkan Fibre Broadband anda.

500Mbps atau 1Gbps tidak akan membaiki laluan antarabangsa yang sedang congestion.

Oleh itu, masalah kelajuan yang dialami pengguna adalah kesan langsung daripada kapasiti trafik antarabangsa yang terhad dan bukan kegagalan perkhidmatan ISP tempatan.

title: 海底光缆维修：为什么国外网站会突然变慢？
content:
如果你发现 马来西亚本地网站正常，但美国、日本或其他海外网站突然变慢，问题不一定出在你家的 Fibre Broadband。

国际海底光缆发生故障或进行维修时，ISP 可用的国际传输容量可能减少。ISP 会把流量转移到其他国际路线，但备用路线可能更长，也可能更加拥堵，因此用户仍然会感受到明显的延迟或速度下降。

为什么马来西亚需要依赖海底光缆？

你的家用 Fibre 并不是直接连接到全球 Internet。

当你访问海外服务器时，数据通常会先经过 ISP 的本地网络，再进入国际网络，最后通过一条或多条海底光缆前往其他国家。

简单来说，一次连接可能经过：

你的家 → ISP 网络 → 国际 Gateway → 海底光缆 → 海外网络 → 目标服务器

如果你访问的是马来西亚本地服务器，流量可能主要留在国内网络。

但如果你访问的是美国、日本或欧洲的服务器，数据就必须经过国际网络。

因此，本地网站正常、海外网站变慢，并不矛盾。

问题可能根本不在你家的 Fibre，而是在 ISP 更上游的国际连接。

海底光缆出问题后，会发生什么？

海底光缆故障并不代表整个 ISP 会马上断网。

更常见的情况是：

某条国际路线的可用容量减少。

大型 ISP 通常不会只依赖一条国际路线。当其中一条 Cable 出现故障时，网络运营商可以把流量转移到其他可用路径。

这就是我们常说的 Rerouting（重新路由）。

例如原本可能是：

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable A → Overseas Transit → Server

Cable A 出现问题后：

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable B → Overseas Transit → Server

用户仍然可以连接到服务器，但 Cable B 的路线可能更长，或者剩余容量没有 Cable A 那么充足。

所以：

Cable 坏了 ≠ Internet 一定断掉。

但：

Rerouting 也 ≠ 原来的速度和延迟完全不变。

APCN2 和 AAG：马来西亚过去就发生过类似情况

马来西亚的国际网络曾受到包括 APCN2 和 AAG 等海底光缆系统故障或维修的影响。

APCN2

Asia Pacific Cable Network 2（APCN2） 是连接亚洲多个主要电信市场的国际海底光缆系统。

在 APCN2 出现故障时，TM 曾表示其国际容量受到影响，但通过其他国际路线进行重新路由和优化，以维持服务。

这其实很好地解释了为什么海底光缆断了，用户却没有完全断网。

原本的 Cable 出问题，但流量被转移到其他路线。

真正的问题变成：备用路线有没有足够容量。

AAG

Asia-America Gateway（AAG） 是连接东南亚与包括美国、香港等地区的重要海底光缆系统。

过去 AAG 进行维修时，TM 曾提醒用户，依赖相关国际路线的部分服务可能出现性能下降，同时会把流量转移到其他路线，以减少影响。

所以你会发现，ISP 的 Cable Maintenance 公告通常不会简单写：

“整个 Internet 会变慢。”

因为实际影响取决于哪一条路线受到影响，以及你的流量原本走哪里。

ISP 的 Rerouting 到底是怎么工作的？

这里真正值得理解的，并不是“ISP 找另一条 Cable”这么简单。

Internet 是由大量不同的网络组成，而这些网络之间需要交换路由信息。

在大型 Internet 网络层面，其中一个核心机制就是 BGP（Border Gateway Protocol）。

BGP 用来告诉其他网络：

“哪些 IP Prefix 可以通过我这里到达，以及应该经过什么路径。”

当某条国际路线不可用或网络运营商需要调整流量时，相关路由信息可以发生变化，让流量转向另一条可用路径。

对普通用户来说，可以把它理解为：

目的地没有变，但去目的地的路线变了。

而路线改变之后，最容易受到影响的是三个东西：

Latency

备用路线可能更长，或者经过更多 Network Hops，因此 Ping 增加。

Packet Loss

如果大量流量被挤到备用路线，而备用路线出现拥堵，就可能产生 Packet Loss。

Throughput

TCP 连接检测到丢包或拥塞后，会降低传输速率。

因此，即使你的 Fibre 本身拥有 500Mbps 或 1Gbps 的本地带宽，某个海外下载仍然可能非常慢。

问题不一定是你家的 Fibre Speed 不够，而可能是通往目标服务器的国际路径出现拥塞或丢包。

为什么 Rerouting 后 Internet 还是会变慢？

假设原本的国际路线还有大量空余容量。

一旦某条海底光缆停止服务，原本经过这条 Cable 的流量必须转移到其他路线。

如果备用路线容量足够，普通用户可能几乎感觉不到变化。

但如果大量流量集中到容量有限的路线，就会开始出现拥塞。

这也是为什么 Cable Incident 经常出现一种很奇怪的情况：

凌晨很正常，晚上却特别慢。

因为国际路线在高峰时段本来就有更多流量。

因此，Cable Fault 的表现可能是：

  1. Singapore 网站正常
  2. US 网站很慢
  3. Japan Server Ping 增加
  4. Gaming 延迟突然升高
  5. VPN 连接变得不稳定
  6. 海外下载速度明显下降

这并不一定代表你的 Fibre 本身出现故障。

为什么只有某些网站变慢？

这是判断问题位置时非常重要的一点。

海底光缆故障不会平均影响所有网站。

原因包括：

不同网站使用不同路线

新加坡、日本和美国服务器可能完全使用不同的国际路径。

因此一个国家的服务正常，并不能证明另一个国家的路线也正常。

网站可能使用 CDN

大型平台通常会使用 Content Delivery Network（CDN）。

如果你访问的内容已经缓存到比较靠近马来西亚的节点，就不一定需要一直连接到美国或欧洲的 Origin Server。

所以即使某条跨洲海底光缆出现问题，使用附近 CDN 的服务仍可能运行正常。

不同 ISP 的国际连接不同

即使两个人住在同一个地区，不同 ISP 也可能拥有不同的国际 Upstream 或 Transit 路线。

一个 ISP 可能已经把流量成功转移到比较空闲的路线，而另一个 ISP 的备用路线可能更加拥堵。

所以：

朋友的 ISP 正常，不代表你的 Fibre 一定坏了。

为什么 Speed Test 还是可以跑到 500Mbps？

这是消费者最容易误判的地方之一。

Speed Test 测试的并不是一个叫做 “整个 Internet” 的东西。

它测试的是：

你的设备 → ISP → 指定 Speed Test Server

如果这个测试服务器位于马来西亚，或者你的 ISP 与该服务器之间拥有良好的本地 Peering，那么测试流量根本不需要经过发生问题的国际路线。

所以完全可能出现：

Malaysia Speed Test：500Mbps

同时：

US Website：非常慢

这两个结果并不冲突，因为它们走的是不同的 Network Path。

如果要判断是不是国际网络问题，可以比较不同目的地：

  1. Malaysia
  2. Singapore
  3. Hong Kong
  4. Japan
  5. United States

如果本地速度正常，但多个海外目的地出现明显较高的 Latency 或 Packet Loss，就更值得怀疑国际路线。

想进一步确认？可以用 Traceroute

如果你对网络技术比较熟悉，Traceroute 比单纯看 Speed Test 更有参考价值。

Windows 可以使用：

tracert example.com

macOS 或 Linux：

traceroute example.com

它会显示你的设备到目标服务器之间经过的 Network Hops。

不过不要犯一个常见错误：

看到某一个 Hop 显示 Packet Loss，就直接认定那个 Router 坏了。

部分 Router 本来就可能限制或忽略 ICMP 回应，因此中间某个 Hop 显示丢包，并不一定代表最终连接真的丢包。

更有意义的是看整体路径变化。

例如：

Malaysia → ISP Network → International Gateway → Singapore → US → Destination

如果你发现某个海外目标突然走了完全不同的路径，或者离开 Malaysia 后 Latency 明显增加，这就是比较有价值的线索。

最好同时：

  1. 测试不同海外目的地
  2. 不同时间测试
  3. 比较不同网络

这样比单独跑一次 Traceroute 更有意义。

为什么 Packet Loss 有时比速度下降更严重？

很多用户只看 Mbps，但对于国际连接来说，Latency 和 Packet Loss 同样重要，甚至可能更加明显。

TCP 发现 Packet Loss 后，会认为网络可能存在拥塞或传输问题，并降低发送速度。

因此，即使只有一定程度的持续丢包，也可能明显影响长距离 TCP 连接。

例如你的 Fibre 本地仍然拥有数百 Mbps 的容量，但从 Malaysia 到美国的国际路径出现拥塞和 Packet Loss，那么：

本地 Fibre 速度很快 ≠ 美国服务器下载速度一定快。

这对于以下服务尤其明显：

  1. Cloud Services
  2. International File Downloads
  3. Remote Desktop
  4. VPN
  5. Online Gaming
  6. Video Conferencing

换 ISP 可以解决海底光缆问题吗？

有可能，但绝对不是保证。

关键不是 Broadband Bill 上写着哪个品牌，而是：

这个 ISP 实际上通过什么国际网络到达你的目标服务器。

两个不同的 ISP 可能使用不同的国际路线。

反过来，两个看起来完全不同的 Broadband Service，也可能在某些地方共享相同的 Upstream、Transit 或 Cable Capacity。

因此，如果问题是国际路线拥塞，单纯从：

300Mbps → 500Mbps → 1Gbps

并不会自动解决问题。

如果 Bottleneck 位于国际网络，你增加的是家里的 Access Capacity，而不是那条国际路线的容量。

海底光缆维修需要多久？

没有一个统一的维修时间。

海底光缆维修需要专业的海上维修船只和设备，时间可能受到以下因素影响：

  1. 故障位置
  2. 海况与天气
  3. Repair Vessel 是否可用
  4. 能否进入故障区域
  5. Spare Cable 是否充足
  6. 受影响的 Cable Segment 数量
  7. Cable Owners / Operators 之间的协调

但这里有一个重要区别：

Physical Repair Time ≠ Customer Impact Time

ISP 不一定要等海底光缆实际修好之后，用户的 Internet 才能恢复正常。

如果 ISP 成功把流量转移到其他路线，用户的体验可能在 Cable 完全维修之前就已经改善。

反过来，一条 Cable 即使没有完全断掉，在维修期间降低可用容量，也可能造成拥塞。

怎么判断是家里的 Fibre 还是国际网络出了问题？

不要只看一次 Speed Test，而是看问题出现的模式。

你遇到的情况比较可能的原因
马来西亚和海外网站全部变慢WiFi、Router、Fibre、Access Network 或 ISP 问题
本地网站正常，部分海外网站很慢International Routing / Destination 问题
多个海外国家的 Latency 都突然升高国际连接问题
只有一个网站很慢网站服务器、CDN 或网站本身的问题也可能
不同 ISP 的表现明显不同International Routing / Upstream 不同
Speed Test 正常，但海外下载很慢International Congestion、Packet Loss 或 Server 限制

这不是专业网络工程师的最终诊断，但足以帮助普通用户避免一个最常见的错误：

海外网站慢，就马上怪自己的 Fibre。

海底光缆出现故障时，马来西亚用户应该怎么办？

如果 ISP 已经确认是 International Cable Fault 或 Maintenance，而你家里的本地连接没有其他问题，就没有必要一直重复 Restart ONT 或 Router。

更有效的方法是确认：

  1. 马来西亚本地服务是否正常
  2. 哪些海外网站受到影响
  3. 不同国家的 Server 是否表现不同
  4. Latency 有没有明显增加
  5. 是否出现 Packet Loss
  6. ISP 有没有发布 International Network Incident 公告

如果联系 ISP，也不要只说：

“我的 Internet 很慢。”

最好提供：

  1. 哪个网站
  2. 哪个时间段
  3. 目标国家
  4. Ping / Latency
  5. Traceroute 结果

这些资料对判断问题发生在哪里更有帮助。


NetBijak’s Take

海底光缆故障，不等于你家的 Fibre 坏了。

真正需要判断的是问题发生在哪里：可能是本地 WiFi，也可能是 ISP Access Network，更可能是通往某个海外目的地的 International Route。

如果马来西亚本地服务正常，但特定海外网站突然出现高 Latency、Packet Loss 或明显的 Throughput 下降，那么在升级 Fibre 配套之前，先检查 International Routing。

500Mbps 还是 1Gbps，解决不了一条正在拥堵的国际路线。

🎯为我找配套 →

title: Submarine Cable Repairs: Why International Sites Slow Down Suddenly
content:
When overseas websites suddenly become slow but Malaysian websites and your local speed test still look normal, the problem may not be your Fibre connection at all. A fault or maintenance event affecting an international submarine cable can reduce the capacity available between Malaysia and overseas networks, forcing ISPs to move traffic onto alternative routes.

For Malaysian users, the important question is therefore not simply “Is the cable broken?”, but which route is affected, where your ISP sends the traffic instead, and whether the alternative path is congested.

Why Malaysia Depends on Submarine Cables

Most international Internet traffic cannot travel directly from a Malaysian home to an overseas server. After leaving your ISP's domestic network, the traffic normally enters an international network and eventually crosses one or more submarine cable systems before reaching another country.

This is particularly important for services hosted outside Malaysia. A connection to a Malaysian website may remain largely within domestic infrastructure, while a connection to a server in the US, Japan or Europe requires international transit.

That difference explains a common Malaysian broadband complaint:

Local websites work normally, but certain overseas services suddenly become slow.

It does not necessarily mean the Fibre line between your home and the ISP has degraded. The problem can be further upstream, somewhere along the international path.

What Happens When an International Cable Has a Fault?

A submarine cable fault does not normally disconnect an ISP from the global Internet altogether. The more immediate problem is loss of available capacity on a particular route.

Major ISPs and network operators normally have multiple international connections. When one cable becomes unavailable, traffic can be redirected through another available path.

This process is generally referred to as rerouting.

For example, a simplified route might look like:

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable A → Overseas Transit → Server

After a fault:

Malaysia → International Gateway → Cable B → Overseas Transit → Server

The second route may keep the connection alive, but it may not have the same latency or available capacity as the original route.

This is why users can experience slower overseas websites even though the Internet connection itself has not completely gone down.

APCN2 and AAG: Real Examples Affecting Malaysian Connectivity

Malaysia has experienced international cable incidents before, including faults involving major systems such as APCN2 and AAG.

APCN2

The Asia Pacific Cable Network 2 (APCN2) is an international submarine cable system connecting major telecommunications markets across Asia.

During an APCN2 fault, TM reported that it lost international capacity but was able to reroute traffic through alternative international routes while repair work was underway.

That example is important because it shows why a cable fault does not necessarily produce a nationwide Internet outage.

The physical cable can be damaged while customers remain online because the operator has moved traffic elsewhere.

The trade-off is that the replacement route may have less spare capacity or a different path to the destination.

AAG

The Asia-America Gateway (AAG) is another major submarine cable system connecting Southeast Asia with international destinations including the US.

During previous AAG maintenance, TM warned that users accessing certain services could experience service degradation and said traffic would be diverted through alternative routes to minimise the impact.

This is why cable repair announcements often mention specific destinations or applications rather than saying “the whole Internet will be slow.”

The impact depends on the traffic that normally uses the affected route.

What Does ISP Rerouting Actually Mean?

Rerouting is more than simply finding another physical cable.

Internet traffic is controlled by routing information exchanged between networks. At the larger Internet level, BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is used by autonomous systems to advertise which IP prefixes they can reach and through which paths.

If an international path becomes unavailable, routing information can change so that traffic is directed through another available path.

The exact process differs between networks, but the practical result for a consumer is straightforward:

The destination is still reachable, but the path used to reach it has changed.

That change can affect three things that matter to users:

  1. Latency: the new path may travel through more network hops or a less direct geographic route.
  2. Packet loss: congestion or instability on the alternative route can cause packets to be dropped.
  3. Throughput: TCP-based applications reduce their sending rate when they detect packet loss, meaning a connection can have plenty of theoretical bandwidth but still deliver poor real-world download performance.

This is one reason a user can see a perfectly respectable speed-test result while an overseas download remains unusually slow.

Why Does Rerouting Sometimes Make the Internet Feel Worse?

Imagine an international route normally operating with plenty of spare capacity.

If a submarine cable suddenly becomes unavailable, its traffic has to be absorbed by the remaining routes.

If those routes have sufficient capacity, most customers may notice little difference.

If they do not, congestion starts to appear.

The result can be particularly noticeable during peak hours, when the alternative international links are already carrying heavy traffic.

This is also why a cable fault can produce inconsistent symptoms. A website may load quickly at 3am but become slow at 9pm. A Singapore service may work normally while a US service performs badly. A gaming connection may suffer high ping while ordinary web browsing remains usable.

These differences are clues about where the bottleneck may be.

Why Are Some Websites Slow While Others Work Normally?

A submarine cable fault does not affect every Internet destination equally.

There are several reasons.

The destination may use a different route

Two websites hosted in different countries can take completely different paths out of Malaysia.

A Singapore-hosted service may use a regional route that is unaffected, while a US-based service may depend on an international path experiencing congestion.

The service may use a CDN

Large platforms often distribute content through Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).

If the content is served from a nearby cache, your traffic may not need to travel to the company's original server in the US or Europe.

That can make a major difference during an international routing incident.

Different ISPs may use different upstream paths

Even when two customers are physically located next to each other, their ISPs may have different international connectivity arrangements.

One ISP may have a less congested alternative route available, while another may be sending more traffic through an overloaded path.

This is why “my friend's Internet is fine” does not automatically mean your Fibre line is faulty.

Why Can a Speed Test Still Show 500Mbps?

This is where many consumers misdiagnose the problem.

A speed test does not measure “the Internet” as one single connection. It measures the path between your device and a particular test server.

If the test server is in Malaysia or connected through a strong local peering arrangement, your traffic may never touch the international route causing the problem.

You could therefore see:

500Mbps to a Malaysian test server

while experiencing:

slow downloads from a US server

Both results can be accurate because they are testing different network paths.

For troubleshooting, it is more useful to compare destinations.

Test a Malaysian server first, then compare services or servers in places such as:

  1. Singapore
  2. Hong Kong
  3. Japan
  4. United States

If local connectivity remains healthy but certain international destinations show significantly higher latency or packet loss, the problem is more likely to be related to the international path rather than your Wi-Fi speed.

Use Traceroute to See Where the Path Changes

For technically minded users, traceroute can provide more useful information than a single speed-test number.

On Windows, you can use:

tracert example.com

On macOS or Linux:

traceroute example.com

The command shows the network hops between your device and the destination.

You are not necessarily looking for one specific hop to “blame”. Internet routers may deliberately hide ICMP responses, and some intermediate hops can show packet loss without actually affecting the final connection.

Instead, look for patterns.

For example:

Malaysia → ISP network → International Gateway → Singapore → US → Destination

If an international route suddenly takes a noticeably different path, or latency increases substantially after traffic leaves Malaysia, that provides useful evidence that the problem is occurring beyond your home network.

A proper diagnosis should compare the results with another destination and, ideally, with results taken at different times.

Why Packet Loss Can Hurt More Than a Lower Speed

Users often focus on Mbps, but international applications can be much more sensitive to latency and packet loss.

For TCP connections, packet loss signals congestion or transmission problems. TCP responds by reducing its sending rate and then gradually increasing it again.

That means even a relatively small amount of sustained packet loss can have a disproportionate effect on a long-distance connection.

For example, a Fibre plan may still have hundreds of Mbps of available capacity locally, but a congested international path with packet loss can make a large overseas file download perform far below expectations.

This is particularly noticeable with:

  1. Cloud services
  2. International file downloads
  3. Remote desktops
  4. VPN connections
  5. Online gaming
  6. Video conferencing

The problem is not necessarily “insufficient Fibre speed.” It can be the quality of the route between the ISP and the destination.

Can Changing ISP Fix a Submarine Cable Problem?

Sometimes, but there is no guarantee.

The important factor is not the brand printed on your broadband bill. It is the ISP's actual international connectivity.

Two retail broadband providers may use different international routes, while two apparently different services may share some upstream infrastructure or cable capacity.

This means switching from one ISP to another is only useful if the new provider gives you a meaningfully different route to the affected destination.

It is also why upgrading from 300Mbps to 500Mbps or 1Gbps does not automatically solve an international routing problem.

If the bottleneck is upstream, buying more domestic access bandwidth does not create additional international capacity.

How Long Do Submarine Cable Repairs Take?

There is no universal repair time.

A damaged submarine cable requires specialised marine repair work, and the timeline can depend on:

  1. The location of the fault
  2. Weather and sea conditions
  3. Availability of a cable repair vessel
  4. Access to the damaged section
  5. Spare cable availability
  6. The number of cables or segments involved
  7. Coordination between cable system owners and operators

However, physical repair time and customer impact are not the same thing.

An ISP may restore acceptable connectivity by rerouting traffic before the damaged cable is physically repaired.

Conversely, a cable may remain operational but have reduced capacity during maintenance, producing noticeable congestion without a complete outage.

That distinction is often missing from consumer discussions about submarine cable incidents.

How to Tell If the Problem Is Your Fibre or the International Network

Use the pattern of the problem rather than relying on one speed test.

What you experienceWhat it may indicate
Malaysian and overseas websites are all slowHome network, Wi-Fi, access network or ISP issue
Malaysian websites work normally but certain overseas sites are slowInternational routing or destination issue
Several overseas destinations show higher latencyWider international connectivity problem
Only one website is slowWebsite/CDN/server problem is also possible
Different ISP users experience different performanceDifferent routing or upstream connectivity
Speed test is normal but overseas download is slowDifferent path, congestion, packet loss or server-side limitation

This is not a substitute for an ISP network diagnosis, but it helps prevent the common mistake of blaming the Fibre line simply because one overseas website is slow.

What Should Malaysian Users Do During a Cable Incident?

If your ISP has announced a submarine cable fault or international maintenance, there is usually little value in repeatedly restarting the ONT or router unless you are also experiencing local connectivity problems.

Instead, establish whether the issue is actually international.

Start with a Malaysian speed test or local service. Then test the overseas service that is giving you trouble. If possible, compare several destinations and run a traceroute to identify whether the route changes after leaving your ISP's local network.

If the ISP confirms an international cable incident, the most useful information is usually the affected route, expected service impact and whether traffic has already been rerouted.

Do not assume that a higher-speed broadband package will fix the problem. International routing and last-mile Fibre speed are separate parts of the connection.


NetBijak's Take

A submarine cable fault is not the same thing as a Fibre outage at your home.

The important distinction is where the congestion or failure occurs. Your local Fibre connection can remain perfectly healthy while an international route is operating with reduced capacity, forcing your ISP to reroute traffic through a longer or more congested path.

For Malaysian consumers, the practical lesson is simple: check the destination and the route before blaming your broadband speed. If local services remain normal while specific overseas destinations suddenly develop high latency, packet loss or poor throughput, an international connectivity problem is a much stronger suspect than a faulty home router.
